title: Transport of a vertical square-pasting equation through coherent comparisons
statement:
Let $A,B,C,D,E,F$ and $A',B',C',D',E',F'$ be categories, with functors $E_X:X\to X'$ for the six corresponding pairs. Let $K:A\to B$, $I:C\to D$, $J:E\to F$, $P_1:D\to B$, $P_2:F\to D$, $P_{12}:F\to B$, $R_1:C\to A$, $R_2:E\to C$, $R_{12}:E\to A$, and let primed functors have the corresponding primed endpoints. A cell is a natural transformation. For a cell $t:T\to U$, the whiskerings $Ht$ and $tG$ have components $H(t_N)$ and $t_{G(N)}$, respectively. No adjunctions are required. For functors $E_X:X\to X'$ and $F:X\to Y$ equipped with an invertible natural comparison $e_F:E_YF\simeq F'E_X$, put $e_{HF}=(H'e_F)\circ(e_HF)$ for a composite $HF$. For a cell $t:F\to H$ with the same endpoints, say it is respected if $e_H\circ E_Y(t)=(t'E_X)\circ e_F$. All compositions below are in the usual right-to-left order, with the canonical functor associators inserted. Choose comparisons $e_K,e_I,e_J,e_{P_1},e_{P_2},e_{P_{12}},e_{R_1},e_{R_2},e_{R_{12}}$. Let $c_P:P_{12}\simeq P_1P_2$, $c_R:R_{12}\simeq R_1R_2$ and primed counterparts satisfy $e_{P_1P_2}\circ E_B(c_P)=(c'_PE_F)\circ e_{P_{12}}$ and $e_{R_1R_2}\circ E_A(c_R)=(c'_RE_E)\circ e_{R_{12}}$. Let $a:P_1I\to KR_1$, $b:P_2J\to IR_2$, $c:P_{12}J\to KR_{12}$ and primed counterparts be respected cells. If
$$ (a'R'_2)\circ(P'_1b')\circ(c'_PJ')=(K'c'_R)\circ c',$$
then for every $N\in E$,
$$ E_B\big(((aR_2)\circ(P_1b)\circ(c_PJ))_N\big)=E_B\big(((Kc_R)\circ c)_N\big).$$
No faithfulness or equivalence of $E_X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose); agent categorical transport argument, isolating ordinary_vertical_transport in lean/Sheaf/AlgebraicGeometry/VaryingRingProperOpenPasting.lean; the tag motivates the pasting shape, not this abstract transport theorem

proof.text:
Fix $N\in E$ and put $x=E_E(N)$. Write $E_B(f)$ for the image of a morphism $f$ and suppress $\circ$ between morphisms (rightmost first). For any composable pair $H,G$, the stipulated comparison has component
$$e_{HG,N}=H'(e_{G,N})e_{H,G(N)}.$$
Use this formula iteratively to define
$$u=e_{P_{12}J,N},\quad q=e_{P_1P_2J,N},\quad z=e_{P_1IR_2,N},\quad v=e_{KR_1R_2,N},\quad w=e_{KR_{12},N}.$$
For example $v=K'R'_1(e_{R_2,N})K'(e_{R_1,R_2N})e_{K,R_1R_2N}$. The two parenthesizations give this same expression by preservation of composition. The canonical functor associators have identity components, so all subsequent component equations also hold with the statement's associators inserted. Each of $u,q,z,v,w$ is invertible: functors send an inverse to an inverse, and the inverse of a composite is the reverse composite of inverses.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 1: comparison components

proof.text:
Transport the initial compositor. Expand $q=P'_1P'_2(e_{J,N})e_{P_1P_2,JN}$ and $u=P'_{12}(e_{J,N})e_{P_{12},JN}$. The assumed $c_P$ comparison at $JN$, followed by naturality of $c'_P$ at $e_{J,N}:E_F(JN)\to J'x$, gives the three-line calculation
$$\begin{aligned}
qE_B(c_{P,JN})
&=P'_1P'_2(e_{J,N})c'_{P,E_F(JN)}e_{P_{12},JN}\\
&=c'_{P,J'x}P'_{12}(e_{J,N})e_{P_{12},JN}
=c'_{P,J'x}u.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus the whiskered compositor has the required comparison, without assuming the realization functors faithful.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 2: left compositor

proof.text:
Transport the middle factor. Naturality of $e_{P_1}$ at $b_N:P_2JN\to IR_2N$ says
$$e_{P_1,IR_2N}E_B(P_1(b_N))=P'_1(E_D(b_N))e_{P_1,P_2JN}.$$
Expand $z=P'_1(e_{IR_2,N})e_{P_1,IR_2N}$ and $q=P'_1(e_{P_2J,N})e_{P_1,P_2JN}$. Substituting the displayed naturality equation and then the respected-cell hypothesis $e_{IR_2,N}E_D(b_N)=b'_xe_{P_2J,N}$ yields
$$\begin{aligned}
zE_B(P_1(b_N))
&=P'_1(e_{IR_2,N}E_D(b_N))e_{P_1,P_2JN}\\
&=P'_1(b'_x)P'_1(e_{P_2J,N})e_{P_1,P_2JN}
=P'_1(b'_x)q.
\end{aligned}$$

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 3: middle whiskering

proof.text:
Transport the last factor. Expand $v=K'R'_1(e_{R_2,N})e_{KR_1,R_2N}$ and $z=P'_1I'(e_{R_2,N})e_{P_1I,R_2N}$. Respect for $a$ at $R_2N$ gives the first equality below; naturality of $a':P'_1I'\to K'R'_1$ at $e_{R_2,N}:E_C(R_2N)\to R'_2x$ gives the second:
$$\begin{aligned}
vE_B(a_{R_2N})
&=K'R'_1(e_{R_2,N})a'_{E_C(R_2N)}e_{P_1I,R_2N}\\
&=a'_{R'_2x}P'_1I'(e_{R_2,N})e_{P_1I,R_2N}
=a'_{R'_2x}z.
\end{aligned}$$
Only $a'$ is used as a natural transformation; neither $a$ nor $a'$ is required to be invertible.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 4: right whiskering

proof.text:
For the other path, respect for $c$ is exactly
$$wE_B(c_N)=c'_xu.$$
Set $r=e_{R_1R_2,N}$. Naturality of $e_K$ at $c_{R,N}:R_{12}N\to R_1R_2N$ and the assumed $c_R$ comparison $rE_A(c_{R,N})=c'_{R,x}e_{R_{12},N}$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
vE_B(K(c_{R,N}))
&=K'(r)e_{K,R_1R_2N}E_B(K(c_{R,N}))\\
&=K'(rE_A(c_{R,N}))e_{K,R_{12}N}\\
&=K'(c'_{R,x})K'(e_{R_{12},N})e_{K,R_{12}N}
=K'(c'_{R,x})w.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality uses the explicit formula for $v$ from Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 5: outer cell and right compositor

proof.text:
Put $L_N=a_{R_2N}P_1(b_N)c_{P,JN}$ and $H_N=K(c_{R,N})c_N$. Preservation of composition by $E_B$, followed by the three equations in Steps 4, 3 and 2, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
vE_B(L_N)
&=a'_{R'_2x}zE_B(P_1(b_N))E_B(c_{P,JN})\\
&=a'_{R'_2x}P'_1(b'_x)qE_B(c_{P,JN})\\
&=a'_{R'_2x}P'_1(b'_x)c'_{P,J'x}u.
\end{aligned}$$
Similarly the two equations in Step 5 give
$$vE_B(H_N)=K'(c'_{R,x})wE_B(c_N)=K'(c'_{R,x})c'_xu.$$
All compositions have common source $E_B(P_{12}JN)$ and target $K'R'_1R'_2x$.

source.place: Tag 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose), vertical-pasting shape only; agent component calculation: 6: compose the component equations

proof.text:
Evaluate the assumed primed pasting identity at $x$:
$$a'_{R'_2x}P'_1(b'_x)c'_{P,J'x}=K'(c'_{R,x})c'_x.$$
The two calculations of Step 6 therefore imply $vE_B(L_N)=vE_B(H_N)$. Compose on the left with the inverse of $v$ from Step 1 and use associativity and the identity laws to obtain $E_B(L_N)=E_B(H_N)$. These are precisely the two components in the conclusion. The object $N$ was arbitrary; no property of any $E_X$ beyond functoriality was used.
